name: General Aptitude
syllabus: Verbal Aptitude (grammar, vocabulary, reading comprehension, verbal analogies), Quantitative Aptitude (data interpretation, ratios, percentages, permutations & combinations, geometry, mensuration, series, logarithms), Analytical Aptitude (logic, deduction, induction, analogy, number relations) and Spatial Aptitude (transformation of shapes, paper folding, cutting, patterns).
note: Exactly 15 marks every year (5 one-mark + 5 two-mark). Do 30 minutes of PYQs daily alongside other subjects.

name: Probability & Statistics
syllabus: Counting (permutations and combinations), probability axioms, sample space, events, independent events, mutually exclusive events, marginal, conditional and joint probability, Bayes theorem, conditional expectation and variance, mean, median, mode and standard deviation, correlation and covariance, random variables, discrete random variables and probability mass functions, uniform, Bernoulli, binomial distribution, continuous random variables and probability distribution function, uniform, exponential, Poisson, normal, standard normal, t-distribution, chi-squared distributions, cumulative distribution function, conditional PDF, central limit theorem, confidence interval, z-test, t-test, chi-squared test.
topics: Discrete distributions: uniform, Bernoulli, binomial, Poisson
Conditional expectation & law of total variance
note: Largest maths block; never below 13 marks. Bayes' theorem has appeared every year.

name: Linear Algebra
syllabus: Vector space, subspaces, linear dependence and independence of vectors, matrices, projection matrix, orthogonal matrix, idempotent matrix, partition matrix and their properties, quadratic forms, systems of linear equations and solutions; Gaussian elimination, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, determinant, rank, nullity, projections, LU decomposition, singular value decomposition.
topics: Systems of linear equations & Gaussian elimination
note: Volatile (8 to 17 marks). Eigenvalues have appeared every year.

name: Calculus & Optimization
syllabus: Functions of a single variable, limit, continuity and differentiability, Taylor series, maxima and minima, optimization involving a single variable.
topics: Gradient descent as an update rule

name: Programming, DS & Algorithms
syllabus: Programming in Python, basic data structures: stacks, queues, linked lists, trees, hash tables; search algorithms: linear search and binary search, basic sorting algorithms: selection sort, bubble sort and insertion sort; divide and conquer: mergesort, quicksort; introduction to graph theory; basic graph algorithms: traversals and shortest path.
note: The most stable subject in the paper.

name: DBMS & Warehousing
syllabus: ER-model, relational model: relational algebra, tuple calculus, SQL, integrity constraints, normal form, file organization, indexing, data types, data transformation such as normalization, discretization, sampling, compression; data warehouse modelling: schema for multidimensional data models, concept hierarchies, measures: categorization and computations.
topics: ER model & relational model, keys, integrity constraints
SQL: joins, GROUP BY / HAVING, nested queries
Data types & data transformation (normalization, discretization, sampling, compression)
Data warehousing: star/snowflake schema, OLAP, concept hierarchies, measures
note: Spiked to 18 marks in 2026. An SQL or normalization question has appeared every year.

name: Machine Learning
syllabus: Supervised learning: regression and classification problems, simple linear regression, multiple linear regression, ridge regression, logistic regression, k-nearest neighbour, naive Bayes classifier, linear discriminant analysis, support vector machine, decision trees, bias-variance trade-off, cross-validation methods such as leave-one-out (LOO) and k-folds cross-validation, multi-layer perceptron, feed-forward neural network. Unsupervised learning: clustering algorithms, k-means/k-medoid, hierarchical clustering, top-down, bottom-up: single-linkage, multiple-linkage, dimensionality reduction, principal component analysis.
topics: Linear regression: simple, multiple, ridge (and lasso)
Evaluation metrics: confusion matrix, precision, recall, F1, ROC
Decision trees: entropy, information gain, Gini

name: Artificial Intelligence
syllabus: Search: informed, uninformed, adversarial; logic: propositional, predicate; reasoning under uncertainty: conditional independence representation, exact inference through variable elimination, and approximate inference through sampling.
topics: Uninformed search: BFS, DFS, UCS, IDDFS
Informed search: greedy best-first, A*, admissibility & consistency
note: Volatile (3 to 11 marks), but the search and logic questions are cheap marks.
